title: Traffic tethering and fallout escape hatch brief
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, field-ready brief for a midweek windowed rollout where traffic tethering is required to avoid downstream overload and we need a clearly documented escape hatch for fallout. Intended audience: release conductor, oncall, SRE, product owner.

Goals
- safely move traffic to new serving variant without violating P99 latency SLOs or exceeding quota budgets
- surface regressions within the first 30 minutes of canary to enable fast rollback
- provide a single, low-friction escape hatch path that any operator can execute

When to use this doc
- midweek or weekend non-urgent launches with predictable traffic shape
- feature flips that rely on model routing or regional capacity changes
- experiments where we anticipate small regressions but want automated throttles

High-level plan
1) Preflight (48–6h before): validate capacity and smoke in staging, bump canary config in staging->prod mirror, sanity-check rollout automation.
2) Window start (T0): open 15-minute warmup lane (0.1% traffic) with tethered ramp watchers on duty.
3) Active ramp (T0+15m to T0+90m): step traffic: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20%; hold at each step for telemetry check.
4) Stabilize (T0+90m to T0+240m): continue progressive ramp to desired target, or trigger escape hatch on regression.
5) Post-rollout (T0+24h): run evaluation prompt set, compare quality metrics and cost delta.

Preflight checklist (48–6h) — quick ticks
- [ ] Capacity report: confirm GPU slot headroom in each target region (link to sheet).
- [ ] Dependency freeze: no infra changes in 24h before T0.
- [ ] Canary images built + PR verified: PR merged and image present in registry.
- [ ] Canary config committed: routing policy, TTLs, and cache warming mode recorded.
- [ ] Rollout owner and secondary assigned in calendar + Slack.
- [ ] Pager rotations: ensure SRE oncall aware and available for T0 -> T0+3h.
- [ ] Communication draft: updated release notes and status channel message ready.

Window day quick timeline (hour-of)
- T minus 60m: final smoke in production canary lane with synthetic requests.
- T minus 30m: status check with SRE and product owner; confirm telemetry dashboards preloaded.
- T minus 10m: set rolling snapshot of old config, pin fallback model variants.
- T0: launch 0.1% warmup.
- T0+15m: telemetry review (errors, latency, tail latency, 95/99).
- T0+30m: if green, move to 1%. If red, execute escape hatch.
- T0+60m: move to 5% and run end-to-end user journey smoke.
- T0+90m: if green, bump to 20% and start cost burn sampling.
- T0+240m: reach steady-state target or continue controlled ramp per product ask.

Telemetry & health signals (what to look at)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 per-route and per-region (auto-snapshot comparisons).
- Error rate: 5xx, 4xx spikes, and model-run exceptions.
- Quality regressions: specific evaluation prompts (list below) — check scoring function drop > 4 points.
- Resource signals: GPU mem pressure, NVLink errors, OOMs, disk IO spikes.
- Cost delta: tokens-per-request and tokens-per-call moving average.
- User-visible: percent of small business traffic with degraded UX (if applicable).

Escape hatch (immediate rollback path)
- Trigger conditions (any one triggers hatch):
  - p99 increased > 40% compared to baseline and tail errors > 2x baseline for 10m
  - fatal model exceptions / KV cache corruption observed
  - core dependency outage (e.g., embeddings-store)
- Immediate actions (operator checklist):
  - Step 1: Send “escape hatch” alert in #release-ops with tags @oncall @prod-sec (template below).
  - Step 2: Pause routing automation and set traffic to pinned fallback config (route policy: previous-stable).
  - Step 3: Execute rollout rollback job (link prefixed) and monitor for 5m for stabilization.
  - Step 4: If rollback fails, escalate to SRE primary and exec on emergency hotfix plan.
  - Step 5: Document incident in the release notes draft and assign follow-up tickets.

Communication templates
- Immediate notify (Slack)
  "Escape hatch executed for <release-id> at <time>. Rolling back to previous-stable; monitoring. Owners: <owner> / <secondary>. Observed: increased p99 and model exceptions. Running rollback job: <link>."
- Status update after rollback
  "Rollback complete. Traffic stable at previous-stable. No data loss; impact window: ~XXm. Investigating root cause; triage ticket: RE-4123."

Release notes draft (bullet skeleton)
- Short summary: what changed (one line).
- Why: reason and expected benefits.
- Rollout details: percentage ramp, regions, time window.
- Monitoring: telemetry dashboards and runbooks linked.
- Known issues: initial caveats and followups (tickets).
- Rollback history: if escape hatch used, brief timeline + root-cause link.

Sample canary evaluation prompts (run at each hold step)
- Prompt set A: 12 deterministic queries targeting tokenization/stop-seq behavior.
- Prompt set B: 8 conversational completions that exercise retrieval/tool-calling surface.
- Prompt set C: 6 safety/guardrail probes.
- Pass criteria: automated scorer pass rate >= 95% vs baseline for Prompt set A/B; safety violations = 0.

Open questions / risks
- Do we have an automated way to rewind KV cache state if partial rollout causes cache divergence? (action: eng-serving-runtime to confirm)
- Time to run full evaluation set under throttled canary — currently ~14m for current prompt corpus; need faster micro-bench corpus.
- What is the cost threshold where product wants to pause ramp (e.g., 3x cost)? Decide in preflight.

Post-release actions (T0+24h -> 7d)
- Re-run full eval suite and post diff to the release ticket.
- Collect user journey synthetic traces and compare CTR/engagement (if applicable).
- Schedule 2d retro with product, SRE, and ML leads to review anomalies.
- Create follow-up tickets for perf regression fixes and experiment-level tuning.

Appendix: quick commands and links
- Rollback job (k8s job link): <internal-runbook-link>/jobs/rollback-release-{{id}}
- Telemetry dashboard: <grafana-link>/d/latency-release/rollout-overview
- Canary image registry: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/release-variants/<tag>

Notes to self (scratch)
- If we expect region-specific saturation, add regional ramp guard at 5% per-region.
- Consider prefix caching warmers 1h before T0 for high-cost prompt families.
- Keep sample size of prompt evaluation small but representative for 15m hold checks.
- After successful rollout, update the rollout-calendar template with actual timings + lessons.

Triage tickets to create if hatch executed
- RE-4123: immediate triage (owner: Ravi)
- RE-4124: perf regression followup (owner: Claire)
- RE-4125: KV cache divergence investigation (owner: Omar)

End of brief. Keep this doc as the short-run checklist for any tethered rollout; expand into full playbook if used more than twice in a quarter.
